# kudasai

> kudasai is a small Go CLI that reads a `.kudasai.json` file from the current
> directory and runs the command you name. It gives a team one shared, versioned
> place to define the commands a repository actually needs, so `kudasai test`
> means the same thing for everyone who checks the code out.

Homepage: https://vibaiher.github.io/kudasai/
Source: https://github.com/vibaiher/kudasai
License: GPL

The name is Japanese: ください (kudasai) is the polite imperative, roughly
"please". `kudasai build` reads as "build, please".

## Installation

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vibaiher/kudasai/main/install.sh | sh

or, with Go installed:

    go install github.com/vibaiher/kudasai@latest

Binaries are published for linux and darwin, on amd64 and arm64.

## Configuration

kudasai reads `.kudasai.json` from the current working directory. Commands are
defined under a top-level `commands` object, in either of two forms, which may
be mixed in the same file:

    {
      "commands": {
        "deploy": "git push origin main",
        "test": {
          "run": "go test -v ./tests/...",
          "description": "Run unit tests"
        }
      }
    }

The string form is the shell command. The object form takes `run` (required)
and `description` (optional). Descriptions appear in `--help` and `--json`.

There is one built-in command, `start`. A custom command of the same name
overrides it.

## Execution model

The command string is passed to `sh -c` and runs in the current working
directory. Stdin, stdout and stderr are connected to the terminal, so
interactive commands work. The exit code of the executed command is propagated
to the caller.

## Passing arguments

Arguments given after the command name are shell-quoted and substituted.

- If the command string contains no placeholder, arguments are appended at the
  end. `kudasai test -run TestFoo` runs `go test -v ./tests/... -run TestFoo`.
- `$@` is replaced by all arguments, in order.
- `$1`, `$2`, ... `$N` are replaced by the corresponding positional argument.
  A placeholder with no matching argument resolves to an empty string.

## Built-in flags

All built-in behaviour is behind a `--` flag, so every other name is free for
custom commands.

- `--help` — list available commands with their descriptions
- `--version` — print the installed version
- `--init` — scaffold a `.kudasai.json`, detecting the project type; asks for
  confirmation before writing
- `--init --force` — scaffold over an existing `.kudasai.json`
- `--check` — validate the config file and report how many commands it defines
- `--json` — print the commands as structured JSON

## Project detection used by --init

The first marker file found decides the template: `go.mod` (Go),
`package.json` (Node.js), `Gemfile` (Ruby), `composer.json` (PHP),
`pyproject.toml` then `requirements.txt` (Python). Each template defines
`build`, `start`, `test` and `lint`. If no marker is found, a placeholder
template is written.

## Discovering commands programmatically

`kudasai --json` is the intended entry point for coding agents. It prints:

    {
      "commands": {
        "build": {
          "run": "go build -o kudasai main.go",
          "description": "Build the binary"
        },
        "start": { "builtin": true }
      }
    }

Built-in commands are marked `"builtin": true` and carry no `run` field. To
make this discoverable, add to the repository's agent context file
(`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`):

    Run `kudasai --json` to discover available commands in this repository.
    Use `kudasai <command>` to execute them.
